class.name: TerrainHeightmap
class.brief_description: A serializable grid of terrain heights and vertex colors.
class.description: Stores a rectangular grid of height samples and vertex colors for [HeightmapTerrain3D]. Samples are laid out in row-major order, with [code]z * width + x[/code] indexing. Coordinates of brush methods are in grid cells, not world units. This is a simple heightmap implementation intended for small landscapes; it does not yet support virtual textures, chunked terrain streaming, or LOD. [b]Note:[/b] Multiple nodes can share the same resource. Editing shared heightmap data updates all subscribers.

method.name: apply_color_brush
method.description: Paints vertex colors using linear radial falloff. Strength is clamped to the range [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code].

method.name: apply_height_brush
method.description: Adds [param amount] to the center sample and less to nearby samples, using linear falloff. Negative values lower the terrain. The brush radius must be positive.

method.name: get_color
method.description: Returns the color stored at the given sample.

method.name: get_height
method.description: Returns the height at the integer sample position.

method.name: import_height_image
method.description: Sets grid dimensions from the supplied uncompressed image. Grayscale or single-channel images use the red channel; RGB images use luminance. Values are clamped to [code]0.0[/code]–[code]1.0[/code] and mapped between [param min_height] and [param max_height]. Images must be between 2 and 513 pixels on each axis.

method.name: sample_height
method.description: Returns bilinearly interpolated height. Positions outside the grid are clamped to the nearest edge.

method.name: set_dimensions
method.description: Resizes the grid while preserving the overlap of old and new samples. New heights are zero and new vertex colors are white.

method.name: set_height
method.description: Changes one height sample, triggering mesh rebuilds for all subscribed nodes.

members.member: Row-major vertex color samples. The count must equal [member width] multiplied by [member depth].
